TRIAD PROGRESSIONS

Triad progressions can be more difficult to analyze because the playing field is somewhat leveled. For instance, in major scale triad harmony, there are now three major chords (I, IV, and V), three minor chords (ii, iii, and vi), and one diminished chord (vii°). The same goes for minor keys, but in different categories: three minor triads: i-iv-v; three major triads: Pill, bVI, and bVII; and one diminished: ii°. This means there is no dominant seventh “give-away” chord. With patience and practice, however, triad progressions won't be any more difficult to decipher than seventh chord progressions.
